findings.title: The duplicate probe self-matches the invoice the same tool call just admitted, so a retry of an identical call becomes a duplicate question, and answering it records a real second invoice
findings.evidence: Driven on clara_l01 as clara_runtime inside ONE transaction I rolled back (client 2bf208ae-960b-4f16-af83-3422971b3edb, author ae6974a7-22d3-418b-8825-d13c79d0ddd9, counterparty 65a7cc3c-5bcc-4f34-877c-b6fb15d25d8d, a fresh reference): PROBE#1 match_count = 0 -> ADMIT#1 invoice 5c9253e2 (replayed false) -> ADMIT#2 under the SAME intent key answers invoice 5c9253e2 replayed TRUE (the door's own idempotency is intact) -> PROBE#2 match_count = 1 and the single match IS 5c9253e2, signals [same_reference, same_total_and_date] (SELF-MATCH true). The tool runs the probe at step 1 and only reaches the admission at step 4, so on that retry it returns duplicateQuestion() instead of the replay receipt. The measured reason the probe cannot tell: clara._trade_invoice_duplicate_matches (prosrc read live) filters on client, kind, counterparty family, a non-terminal Work status and an unreversed entry, and has NO exclusion for the caller's own intent key, logical op or work id. Then the second half: because stableOpKey(ctx.taskId, TOOL, input) hashes record_anyway, the follow-up call carries a DIFFERENT intent key, so ADMIT#3 produced a SECOND invoice 2978eebd with the same reference, document_date and total_cents. The tool's own comment at :884-886 argues the key may hash record_anyway 'because the first call refused nothing and admitted nothing' - true on the question path, false on the retry path proved here.
findings.why_it_matters: A duplicate supplier bill or sales invoice is a durable accounting artifact on a client's books. The estate paid for an idempotent admission door precisely so a retried tool call cannot double a recording; this lane's probe sits in front of that door and defeats it. The lane's own report (#1135, follow-up 5) records that runModelSegmentStepV22 FAILED AFTER 3 RETRIES on a second turn in one session, so a segment retry that re-runs the same tool call with the same input is not hypothetical here.
findings.required_fix: Two changes, either of which alone is insufficient. (a) Ask the admission door first, or exclude this call's own intent key from the probe: clara.probe_trade_invoice_duplicates_for needs a p_intent_key (or p_exclude_work) argument so a recording can never be its own look-alike - and the lane's cell battery needs a retry cell that would have reddened on this. (b) Keep record_anyway OUT of stableOpKey: the two calls of one recording are one recording, and the acknowledgement already carries the fact that the person was asked.
findings.not_covered_by: packages/runtime/tests/chat-turn-v22-trade-invoice.test.mjs (11 cells, none drives a retry) and tests/chat-turn-v22-e2e.mjs leg 2 (two DIFFERENT turns, therefore two different task ids and two different op keys, so it never re-enters the same key).

findings.title: The look-alike question is a tool result with no stop condition, so one model segment can probe, set record_anyway itself and record - while writing a durable row that asserts a person was warned
findings.evidence: stopWhen is [isStepCount(CHAT_STEP_BUDGET=8), hasToolCall("clarify"), stoppedOnTerminalPost] - stoppedOnTerminalPost fires only on POST_TOOL. duplicateQuestion() returns {ok:true, status:'duplicates_found', ...} as an ordinary tool result, so the loop continues and the model may call start_trade_invoice_work again with record_anyway:true inside the SAME segment, up to the step budget. The only wall is prose: chatTurn.v22.prompt.ts:185-192 ('Never record it without asking either. If they say go ahead, call the tool again with record_anyway set'). record_anyway is a plain boolean on the model's own input schema (startTradeInvoiceWorkInputSchemaV2). Meanwhile clara.record_trade_invoice_duplicate_ack writes a durable clara.trade_invoice_duplicate_acks row whose stated purpose, in this file's own comment at :903-904, is 'what lets a reviewer see months later that the preparer was warned and went ahead'.
findings.why_it_matters: CUT-PLAN 1.2 A2 cites claraWork_v4's shape for this ('the shape claraWork_v4 has and chatTurn_v21 does not'), and in v4 a question is clara.open_work_question, which PARKS the run until a person answers. Here nothing parks and nothing stops, so the acknowledgement row can record a human decision no human made. Combined with ADV-C1-01 the duplicate invoice is reachable with no human input at all.
findings.required_fix: Make the look-alike answer end the turn: add a duplicates_found arm to the stop set (alongside stoppedOnTerminalPost), or route the question through the clarify tool that already stops the loop. Whichever is taken, the acknowledgement must only be writable on a turn that follows a human message, and the cell that proves it must drive two segments rather than one.

findings.title: A retried recording writes a SECOND acknowledgement row under one intent key, and the second row's shown[] names the invoice that acknowledgement authorises
findings.evidence: Driven on clara_l01 as clara_runtime inside ONE rolled-back transaction. Planted look-alike X = 396575fb. Call 1 (record_anyway true, intent key K): probe match_count 1 -> ack 976b06f2, shown [396575fb] -> admit Y = 45e0ca51. Retry of the IDENTICAL call (same task, same input, therefore same K): probe match_count 2 -> ack e917b256 (replayed FALSE, a NEW row), shown [396575fb, 45e0ca51] -> admit replays Y. Two acknowledgement rows exist under one intent key, and the second one records that the preparer was shown 45e0ca51 - the very invoice this acknowledgement authorises. The measured reason: clara.record_trade_invoice_duplicate_ack's conflict target is (firm_id, client_id, intent_key, ack_digest) and the digest hashes the shown id array (prosrc read live), so a changed shown list is a new row rather than a replay.
findings.why_it_matters: The row is the audit artifact for 'the preparer was warned'. A second row naming the recording itself is not a warning anyone received; a reviewer reading it months later reads something that did not happen. #1135's walk asserts 'exactly one acknowledgement row' on a path that never retries.
findings.required_fix: Fix the probe first (ADV-C1-01) - excluding this intent key's own work removes the self-naming. Then make the acknowledgement idempotent on (firm, client, intent_key) for this caller, so a retried recording cannot mint a second warning record: either pass the probe's list from the first call, or have the door answer the existing row when the key already carries one.

findings.entry: migration 0321 section A (the widened no-op notion)
findings.title: The widened no-op guard refuses a real invoice.invoice_date correction as value_unchanged, and which correction it refuses depends on the session DateStyle
findings.evidence: Measured on clara_l01 inside rolled-back transactions. Cluster default is DateStyle 'ISO, MDY'. clara._fact_calendar_day('03/05/2026') = 2026-03-05 under MDY and 2026-05-03 under DMY. Consequently clara._fact_value_changed('{"text":"03/05/2026"}','{"text":"2026-03-05"}','invoice.invoice_date') is FALSE under MDY (refused as value_unchanged) and TRUE under DMY, and the mirror pair flips the other way. The two-argument notion 0268 shipped answers TRUE for the same pair (prosrc read live: it compares btrim(text)), so BEFORE 0321 that edit committed and AFTER 0321 it is refused. clara._revisable_invoice_field('invoice.invoice_date') is true and clara._monetary_invoice_field is false, so the new text branch is the one that runs for this field.
findings.why_it_matters: A Malaysian invoice prints 03/05/2026 for 3 May. On this cluster the guard reads it as 5 March, so the bookkeeper who corrects it to 2026-03-05 - a real correction of a genuinely ambiguous printed date - is told 'this revision does not change what the document is recorded as saying', which is false, and their correction is refused with no extraction, no revision row and no retirement. The #1030 report's own AC6 reasoning names exactly this harm pointing the other way ('refusing a real correction is the same defect pointing the other way'); the widening introduced it. The report discloses that _fact_calendar_day is STABLE rather than IMMUTABLE and draws only the indexing consequence, not the semantic one.
findings.required_fix: Pin the parse: add a `set DateStyle = 'ISO, YMD'` clause to clara._fact_calendar_day (it already carries a search_path clause), or restrict the date arm to values that are unambiguous under any DateStyle (an ISO YYYY-MM-DD or a spelled month) and fall through to the text comparison otherwise. Add a cell that drives an ambiguous slash date in both directions.

findings.title: source_moved_again consumes the correction's only op key while the newer correction retires nothing, so the retired Work gets no successor and no surface says so
findings.evidence: Three measured components, not yet driven as one race (the lane's own report says the same: 'the source_moved_again arm is driven only as a pure function; the cell proves the decision, not the race'). (1) rederivedBasis declines source_moved_again whenever b.new_value.cents differs from live_facts[field].cents - i.e. whenever a second correction landed between the retirement and the sweep. (2) The belt settles that decline through clara.settle_source_corrected_rederivation, which reserves the op key through clara._reserve_op; _reserve_op (prosrc read live) raises CLR10 'op_key reused with different args' on any later settlement with a different payload, so the decline is FINAL for that correction. (3) clara._source_corrected_work (prosrc read live) retires only Works with status in ('queued','running','awaiting_input'), no committed receipt and a PENDING clara.agent_interruptions row - so the second correction, arriving while the first Work is already 'cancelled' and no successor exists yet, retires nothing and writes no source_corrected: cancellation receipt, which is the only thing clara.source_correction_rederivations reads. The module's own comment ('The next sweep reads the newest correction and this one is settled by its own successor or decline') does not hold in that case.
findings.why_it_matters: Net effect: the person's instruction is retired, nothing is re-derived, and the only trace is an op_receipt nobody surfaces. #1030's AC4 is 'Needs-you shows the successor's confirmation question after the correction, where before this change it showed nothing' - in this race it shows nothing again, and the lane has shipped a belt that promises otherwise.
findings.required_fix: source_moved_again should not consume the key by declining. The figures already come from live_facts, which IS what the document says now, so the honest answer is to derive from the live reading and admit the successor (the confirmation question then names the current figures), or to settle this key with a decline that the newest reading re-opens. Either way the chain must not be able to end with a retired Work, no successor and no human-visible reason. Drive it with two real connections: retire on revision 1, land revision 2 before the sweep, then sweep.

findings.title: The invoice.currency arm case-folds any text, not only an ISO 4217 code, contrary to the ticket's own per-field rule
findings.evidence: clara._fact_value_changed('{"text":"Ringgit Malaysia"}','{"text":"ringgit malaysia"}','invoice.currency') = false, measured on clara_l01. The date arm is gated on both sides spelling a calendar day; the currency arm has no matching gate on both sides spelling an ISO 4217 code, so free text on that field is folded too.
findings.why_it_matters: The #1030 report's AC6 table states the rule as 'the ISO 4217 code, case-insensitively', and states the opposite rule for anything with no canonical form ('a professional correcting ACME SDN BHD to the mixed case actually printed on the page is making a real correction'). A currency region that carries prose rather than a code gets the wrong one of the two rules.
findings.required_fix: Gate the currency arm the way the date arm is gated: apply the case-insensitive comparison only when both sides match a three-letter alphabetic code (or a real ISO 4217 roster), and fall through to the trimmed-text comparison otherwise.

findings.title: allocations_confirmed is stripped from the wire payload but hashed into the intent key, so two calls differing only in that flag admit two Works for one claim
findings.lines: 1240 (stableOpKey over the whole input), with lib/staff-expense-claim-basis.v2.ts:155-176 (claimFromInputV2 drops the flag)
findings.evidence: Same mechanism as ADV-C1-01, read rather than driven. stableOpKey(ctx.taskId, START_STAFF_EXPENSE_CLAIM_WORK_TOOL, input) hashes the full input; claimFromInputV2 omits allocations_confirmed from p_claim, so two calls produce DIFFERENT intent keys with a byte-identical p_claim. There is no content-level dedupe behind it: clara.admit_staff_expense_claim_work's prosrc contains no _reserve_op and no duplicate check (measured), and clara.staff_expense_claims carries unique indexes only on id, work_id, logical_op_id and corrects_claim_id (pg_indexes, measured). The realistic entry is a single-advance claim sent once without the flag and once with it; a multi-line split is refused locally until the flag is set, so only the confirmed call reaches the door there.
findings.required_fix: Hash the op key over the value that actually goes on the wire - claimFromInputV2's output plus the settlement arm - rather than over the raw tool input, for this tool and for the trade-invoice one. A tool-local flag must not be able to mint a second idempotency key for the same recording.

findings.title: The cell 'record_anyway is TOOL-LOCAL and never reaches the wire' proves only its absence from p_particulars; the flag reaches three durable columns through the intent key
findings.evidence: The cell asserts tradeInvoiceFromInput(bill({record_anyway:true})) deep-equals tradeInvoiceFromInput(bill()) and carries no record_anyway key. It says nothing about stableOpKey, which hashes the flag into p_intent_key - a value that lands durably on clara.accounting_work.intent_key, clara.op_receipts.op_key and clara.trade_invoice_duplicate_acks.intent_key.
findings.required_fix: Either narrow the title to what it proves ('record_anyway is absent from the particulars the door receives') or widen the cell to assert that the intent key is IDENTICAL with and without the flag - which is the assertion that would have caught ADV-C1-01.

findings.title: clara.source_correction_rederivations(int) hands any clara_runtime session every firm's corrections, with the retired basis and the document's live monetary facts
findings.evidence: Driven on clara_l01 as clara_runtime inside a rolled-back transaction: 61 backlog entries across 14 distinct firms and 14 distinct clients in one call, each carrying firm_id, client_id, field_path, prior_value/new_value cents, retired_basis (account codes and memo), retired_source_refs and live_facts. The door is SECURITY DEFINER with no firm argument and no firm predicate; the only bound is the 200-row cap.
findings.why_it_matters: Not a break: it matches the house belt pattern (clara.sweep_intake_batch_cancellations(integer), also clara_runtime, also unscoped), and the belt is a leader singleton that genuinely needs cross-firm reach. It is recorded because it is the widest new read this lane adds, and clara_runtime is the same role the chat lane's ACT pool sets, so any future act-lane tool that could be tricked into calling it would be an estate-wide read.
findings.required_fix: None required for this lane. If the orchestrator wants the posture narrowed, the shape is the estate's own OBO twin: a p_firm argument supplied by the leader's own cycle, or a rig-meta cohort row that pins this door as a deliberately unscoped belt read the way the batch sweep is pinned.

attacks_that_found_nothing: #1000 tenant isolation: clara.wake_get_client_financial_pack resolves the firm from clara.wake_context() (prosrc measured: active membership AND role_rank >= bookkeeper), the core carries an explicit firm predicate at 0320:399-400, and every statement below it is inside the v_visible arm and keyed on p_client. Re-ran client-financial-pack-wake-read.test.mjs with the full gate chain: 10/10, including no_oracle, floor_is_the_credential, grant_is_one_role and read_only.

#1000 SECURITY INVOKER to DEFINER on the human door: checked every relation the core reads (clients, opening_seed_registry, journal_entries, onboarding_plans/items, cash_account_set_versions/members, coa_accounts, journal_lines). All nine are keyed on p_client, and p_clients_human's RLS qual is firm-level only, so the conversion loses no within-firm scoping. The core body carries zero jwt_ reads and zero current_setting calls, and clara.book_today() has no identity dependence.

#985/#986 opening lane: both tools carry the client-in-conversation wall, the bookkeeper+ floor through clara.resolve_chat_principal, the masked 404 for a basis of another client of the same firm, and an F-H7 re-assert immediately before the audited write.
#945 payroll read: clara.get_document_extract is called with the CONVERSATION's client (the three-argument live signature), and the model's client_id is refused if it differs.

#933 (A10) calendar day: the acquired_date text cast is present in loadFaProposalInputsStepV6, so the Asia/Kuala_Lumpur previous-day defect the corrected contract names cannot recur; the step never throws and a failed read yields the v5 question.

Integer cents: proposeAllocationsByDate uses only Math.min and integer subtraction; the accrual per-period arithmetic uses floor/remainder with the remainder pinned to the final due date; prepayment-schedule-basis.ts and revenue-recognition-basis.ts contain no arithmetic at all (the doors compute).
Splice anchors: SYSTEM_PROMPT_V22 is a pure concatenation of v21 plus seven appended stanzas - no string replace, no indexOf, so no anchor can match twice or zero times.

Migration safety on a database with real rows: 0320 is create-or-replace only plus one on-conflict-do-nothing allowlist row; 0321 adds six functions and recuts two bodies, writes no row at apply, and both tails re-derive the pre-images from the LIVE catalog rather than asserting a copy. Both are applied on clara_l01 (311 files).

Lock order in clara.settle_source_corrected_rederivation: retired Work then successor Work, both for update, with the firm taken from the cancellation receipt and never from the caller; a successor of another firm or with a different intent_key is refused with one sentence for both, so the refusal is not an existence oracle. Replay with a different payload is refused CLR10 by clara._reserve_op rather than silently answered.

The registry's five textual shapes: deriveVersionPair + rewriteRegistryToPrevious apply cleanly for chatTurn (v22 to v21), claraWork (v6 to v5) and statementFacts (v3 to v2), so the integrator's two-build drill is not blocked by a formatting slip.

The sixth CLARA_WORK_BUNDLE_V6_BANNER import and console.log landed in commit 411583031, the SAME commit as the registry repoint and claraWorkBundleIdentityV6() in /api/build-info - the last cut's one real defect is not repeated.

CI ordering: clara_rt_test is cut as a template copy at action.yml:201, BEFORE every e2e leg, so the new chat-turn-v22-e2e leg added at :443 cannot contaminate the two-build drill's pristine database.
summary: Nine findings, one blocker. The blocker and the two majors beside it are one family in ticket #1135's A2 (#1007) entry: the duplicate probe runs before the admission door and has no exclusion for the caller's own intent key, so a retry of an identical tool call self-matches, becomes a duplicate question instead of the door's idempotent replay, and - because record_anyway is hashed into the op key - the answer admits a second invoice with the same reference, date and total. All three steps were driven on clara_l01 inside rolled-back transactions. The same retry writes a second acknowledgement row under one intent key whose shown[] names the invoice it authorises, and nothing stops the model from setting record_anyway itself inside a single segment, so the durable row that exists to prove a preparer was warned can record a decision no person made. Ticket #1030 contributes two more: the widened no-op guard now refuses a real invoice.invoice_date correction as value_unchanged and its verdict flips with the session DateStyle (measured both ways), and the source_moved_again decline consumes the correction's only op key in a race where the newer correction retires nothing, leaving a retired Work with no successor and no human-visible reason. Ticket #1000 survived the pass intact: the wake wrapper's firm scope, its bookkeeper+ floor, its no-oracle behaviour and its single grant all held under re-measurement, and the SECURITY INVOKER to DEFINER conversion loses no scoping because every relation the core reads is keyed on the client and the human RLS qual was firm-level only. #985's opening tools, #933's calendar-day cast, the banner, the five registry edits and the freeze/bundle/parity gates all hold.
